items.topic: Jumpr access to rep sales spreadsheets

items.topic: API docs: lead logged at study click
items.statement: Kobi stated that, per the API docs Emily sent (from Ryan), a lead is logged at the time a user clicks a study. He wants to understand how this links back to the rep.
items.quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: they choose the where where you're located and then they go into a study and from the API docs that uh Emily sent from Ryan, / Kobi Kunasekaran: I believe, um it logs a lead at the time that they click a study. / Kobi Kunasekaran: I'm trying to understand like how that links back to the rep.

items.topic: Signup logged once per book
items.statement: Client described the current process: every registration through WagerTech is logged individually per book, so a person who signs up for three books appears three times, each with the live operator.
items.quote: Ali Nawaz: If you look at the bottom there, this is the sign up uh tab, meaning anybody who registers for whatever book through us, uh we have to log each one individually, right? So if they if they signed over three books, their name should be there three times with the operators that were live....

items.topic: One live operator per book per rep
items.statement: Client described the rule: a rep never has two operators live for the same book (for example Proline GD and Proline C). The company can hold multiple deals for one book at the same time, but each rep is assigned one operator per book.
items.quote: Ali Nawaz: ...you will never have two of the same uh you will never have two operators live for the same book. So if it's Proline, you usually wouldn't have Proline GD and Proline C, for example, together, right? It would it would be one.... / Waleed Alasadi: So you said that like you can you can have two pro lines that are active just not active per like a salesperson can only have one active but the company / Ali Nawaz: So I'm Yeah, I'm talking about sales side. Yeah. So company will always have multiple different deals,

items.topic: Target CPA per operator drives rep switches
items.statement: Client described that each operator deal has a target CPA. Ilas, Owen, Lena and the team decide whether to switch high-volume reps to a different operator to hit targets.
items.quote: Ali Nawaz: ...And each operator is given like a target CPA. So depending on if we're close to hitting targets, that's when somebody uh it's actually Ilas and uh Ilas, Owen, and Lena and the team who will decide whether we need to switch one of our high volume reps to a different operator to hit a target or if they're staying....

items.topic: Volume distributed across BAs when deals limited
items.statement: Client described that when deals for a book are limited, volume is split evenly across BAs or assigned to reps who track well; when volume is plentiful, it is broken down by rep volume and trends.
items.quote: Ali Nawaz: ...So we might have four deals for Proline, but there's times where we only have one. And when that happens, we have limits and because of the amount of BAS in the company, uh we have to distribute it in evenly. For example, if one book like MGM, we might have uh temporarily lost the deal and we rely on one. What that means is not everybody could get a a higher amount of volume on it and we have to split it evenly or give assign it accordingly to the people who are tracking well, right? / Ali Nawaz: ...But if it's a book that we have a huge amount of volume or multiple different operators live for Proline, for example, we break it down according to people's volume and different trends, right?...

items.topic: Reps log by operator after switch date
items.statement: Client described that sales reps are only told when they are switched to a different operator, and after the switch date they must log signups under the new operator. Reps check Airtable to see their live books and the date they were changed.
items.quote: Ali Nawaz: ...They're just told when they're switched to a different operator. And what that means is after that date that they're switched, they have to uh they have to make sure they log it by that operator. Now, when we get into Air Table, it that's where they're they're able to see what books they have live and if they're changed, the date they were changed. They cross reference Air Table....

items.topic: Completed signup log fields
items.statement: Client showed the completed signup log: email, date, referral, referral bonus, and a bet credit option where referrals are paid to deposit into a book they registered for through WagerTech.
items.quote: Ali Nawaz: ...so this is how it's logged once it's completed. Right? So, the email, the date, the referral, the referral bonus, right? / Ali Nawaz: There's there's bet credits. There's a bet credit option where people who are referrals, they want they want to get paid for for for them to deposit into one of the books. they registered through us, right? So, beck credits....

items.topic: Three proof screenshots per signup
items.statement: Client described three proofs logged per signup: the welcome email (received once the player is verified), the deposit amount screenshot (exact amount sent), and the transaction/wager history.
items.quote: Ali Nawaz: ...we log three different screenshots here. I mean, this is not this is just general screenshots. And if we wanted more detailed that the the BAS usually have it, but the first one would be this welcome email.... / Ali Nawaz: ...And then uh we this is when we send when we send out that amount they have to deposit it the exact amount and this is where we see that data. If you want to click click one of those again, Andy. Yeah. And then and then transaction history would just be their wager wager history.

items.topic: One account per player per book
items.statement: Client stated a player cannot have more than one account per book; a person who already registered for a book on their own cannot register for it through WagerTech.
items.quote: Ali Nawaz: ...basically you cannot have more than one account for MGM, right? / Ali Nawaz: If you register for MGM yourself in the past, you can't register through us because you've already had an account....

items.topic: Deposit range per deal, BA picks amount
items.statement: Client described that each operator deal has a deposit range (for example 50 to 160) maintained manually in Airtable. The BA picks the amount per client within the range and should vary it. The deposit range is per deal and can change month by month.
items.quote: Ali Nawaz: If you see the deposit range on the bottom, 50 to 160, uh what that means is the BA has the decision to make of how much they want to offer for this one client each time. You want to make sure you switch it up, right? So 50 to 160, but you you have to make sure you're mixing up the ranges there.... / Kobi Kunasekaran: This comes from is this unique per deal or specific or this like / Ali Nawaz: per deal. / Ali Nawaz: doesn't it's always per deal and it could switch month by month and um yeah so it

items.topic: Wager vertical per deal must match
items.statement: Client described that the wagering requirement (sports or casino) depends on the operator deal. If a player registers through a sports link but wagers on casino, it will not track and the CPA does not trigger.
items.quote: Ali Nawaz: ...Caesar CTM has a casino and sports, but sometimes we only have a deal for sports. When that happens, they might have been used to their Caesars's casino uh assignment before, but if once they're switched to the Caesar sports, meaning they'd have to wager in the sports in order for the CB CPAs to trigger and for for it to track. If they register through our sports link and they do casino, it will not track in the system, which is why it's important they they do that correctly, right?

items.topic: PlayCan CMS turns books on/off per rep
items.statement: Client showed PlayCan CMS, where operators/books are turned on and off on each rep's agency site URL. A book is live on a rep's page only if it is live in PlayCan; PlayCan is what runs everything.
items.quote: Ali Nawaz: ...this is our play can CMS. This is where we turn on and off operators, right? So every every person in the company has their own link and site site and agency site with the URL that that's aligned to them. Right? So this is where we turn on and off books.... / Ali Nawaz: The only way it's open live on his page is if it's open live on play can. That's what runs everything, right?...

BAS cannot touch that at all. / Ali Nawaz: No. Yeah. And there's only a few of us who actually uh not the whole ops team like Jay, / Ali Nawaz: myself, Andy, Owen, even Lena and Emily don't they kind of rely on us for that. Uh Jay, so Ashurix is actually Andy, / Ali Nawaz: Andy's a manager. / Ali Nawaz: meaning he has reps under him. / Jay: ...if you have a site, you are a manager. So he has about three or four reps under him. They would also be under the Assurance banner, but they have their own links like they have links that are dedicated to them....

items.quote: Jay: Uh, so it it's both. So like for example, / Jay: if uh Andy puts ashurik.net/alvaro for example, when they go to sign up, Alvaro is already pre-filled in the referral section. So yeah. / Jay: So it's both. It's

items.topic: Only rep's active study links shown
items.statement: Client confirmed that after login and location selection, a player sees only the study links active for that rep at that time; live books differ by rep based on volume and availability.
items.quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: And then when they log in, they're choosing uh where they're located. And then from there, they're they get taken to the study links. And those study links are only the ones that are active for that rep at that like during that time / Jay: Correct. / Ali Nawaz: obviously it might be different links or different books like Andy might have Caesar's sports and Alvaro doesn't have it. So it depends on the rep and their volume and and what we have available at that time...

items.topic: Airtable master links, tracker codes, effective dates
items.statement: Client showed Airtable master links: each operator provides a limited number of links, each with a tracker code used to identify the rep in operator reports, and Airtable records effective from / effective to dates for when a link was live, closed or paused.
items.quote: Ali Nawaz: ...each operator gives us a different amount of links not we might not get 20 links for everything we might / Ali Nawaz: we are able to just identify by that tracker code or the link that it's Andy specifically. And by using air table on the right you'll see like we we have the effective from effective to to let us know when it was live or when it was closed or paused.

items.topic: Airtable first, then PlayCan (fail-safe)
items.statement: Client stated link assignment is done in Airtable first, then activated in PlayCan; Airtable is meant to act as the fail-safe so incorrect links are not put live in PlayCan.
items.quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: So the link assignment and stuff are are you doing it in play can first and then coming to air tableable to update it so um you have like a record or is it the other way around where you're doing everything in air tableable and then you're activating it / Jay: No, it yeah it it would be air table first because um / Jay: air table is supposed to act as the uh as the as the fail safe for play can.

items.topic: Manual PlayCan/Airtable sync discrepancies
items.statement: Client said the process is still manual even with the bot; if someone turns a link on in PlayCan without updating Airtable, discrepancies occur.
items.quote: Ali Nawaz: Uh the problem obviously is that this is still manual work, right? Like there's we have our bot now that helps but it's still manual work. Meaning if somebody was to turn it on play can which is where it actually counts and not update air table then we have we we we might have some discrepancies and we're we're working towards of like limiting that and we don't really have it as much but it's still bound to happen if you're relying on just manual manual changes, right?

items.topic: Rep mislogging after mid-month operator switch
items.statement: Client said BAs switched between operators mid-month often log late-completing signups under the new book, causing inaccurate tracking that ops must investigate using welcome email dates.
items.quote: Ali Nawaz: Because from the from the from the BA standpoint, if they're switched from let's say B proline GD to Proline C in the middle of the month / Ali Nawaz: But we have an issue sometimes with BAS mislogging it. And that's where we have to kind of investigate because they're just doing they're just doing exactly what they're told when they're told whenever they're told to switch to a different operator. But there's a big chance that they got some of them mislogged and then this the tracking numbers don't look accurate until we we review that.

items.topic: Log by welcome email date vs switch date
items.statement: Client explained that signups are supposed to be logged by registration date as shown on the welcome email, compared with the switch date in Airtable; mislogging still happens.
items.quote: Ali Nawaz: Well, they would log it depending on when the person registered, / Ali Nawaz: They would know by the welcome email date would show. If if the if if I was switched from the 15th of June uh to Proline GD and I had Proline C from the 1st to 15th, then if I have a welcome email from Pro June 6, I know that's Proline C because I didn't have it live at that time. / Ali Nawaz: ...So it's kind of a mix of do both, but there's still a lot of mislogging. People don't look they just log things and carelessly sometimes.

That's what I mean. / Kobi Kunasekaran: Um and then right now as I understand like every time they click there's a signup record being created uh by Canon / Ali Nawaz: Yeah. items.topic: Live links per rep vary; NFL peak
items.statement: Client said the number of live links per rep varies (two up to six or seven) and depends on the time of year, with the most volume near NFL season.
items.quote: Jay: It can it could be more than three. / Jay: It can be up to like like six, seven rings, too. / Ali Nawaz: Yeah. It could be it could be two. At sometimes it's two. / Ali Nawaz: I feel like close to like NFL season, that's when we have the most uh volume overall...

items.topic: Owen manages deal updates and extra volume
items.statement: Client said Owen looks into deals and gets updates (with Jess), and lets Ali know when extra volume is available; it is then assigned to BAs who can handle the volume and track well.
items.quote: Ali Nawaz: So that's something actually that Owen deals with where he's the one who looks into the deals or gets updates with Jess. And so when when it comes to what books we have live, they kind of let us let someone like me know and when if we have extra volume available, they let me know. So I mean throughout the month there's always different updates, right? Sometimes we might be limited and it might be they might have got the green light from the operator to to push a little more CPS than we were expected and then we assigned it to the the appropriate BAS who can handle that volume and get the CPAs....

items.topic: Shared links when operators limit supply
items.statement: Client said ideally each rep has their own link to track erosion (signups that did not track), but some operators limit links so multiple reps share one link (for example Caesars D1 shared by six reps). Sharing is tracked in Airtable, and attribution then needs manual log checks.
items.quote: Jay: ...ideally we want each rep to have their own link that way uh we have the most data sets available to us so for example like if Ally has his own link and Andy has his own link and Andy's getting scammed and I can't I'm not going to go blame Alli for Andy Andy tracking because I could because I they have they each have a link. / Jay: ...there's going to be times where we don't have enough links and it's not even like we've tried requesting it from the operators. They just you know they'll say like sorry it's not something that we can give you. Maybe it's because it cost them money. I'm not too sure on the reasoning there but so that we do have uh people who uh will be on the same link and that's also tracked in air table.... / Jay: ...So unfortunately, if one person is getting scammed, we can't, you know, iron iron out who it is. We have to have to go manually check all the logs and stuff....

items.topic: Shared-link attribution via rep slug/site login
items.statement: Kobi proposed that even on a shared link, Salesforce attribution comes from the rep's slug because the player is logged in on that rep's site; Jay agreed the site knows who clicks the link.
items.quote: Jay: ...So that's that's why I was saying for like a sales perspective, it it it would it would be logging it from like on on Salesforce specifically, / Jay: it would it would be logging from that slug from that slug. / Kobi Kunasekaran: Because they'd be logged in, right? / Jay: Yeah, that is correct. / Kobi Kunasekaran: And then even if they're clicking the same shared link, I I think in the / Jay: It doesn't matter because the site would know. The site would know who's clicking the link.

But for some reason, / Jay: ...playan CMS is so archaic and old like this uh the CRM it's so like archaic and old that it doesn't have the ability to to to do that but like like you know um Salesforce is actually a CRM itself and that's why we're moving there...

items.topic: Bot-assisted link reassignment with confirmation
items.statement: Andy described the bot: when moving a rep between operators, it finds the rep's last used or available link, handles link sharing if links are short, and asks for confirmation before changes. Ops then manually copies the link into PlayCan.
items.quote: Andy Bhiekham: ...If you're using the bot, the bot would literally if we're moving a rep from one code to the next or one um let's just say I I'm being moved from Bet MGM um GD to bet NGM CTM, the bot would look for the most uh least the last used uh link and put me on that last used link. Obviously, you confirm before it proceeds, but the bot would kind of sift through what available links there are um and kind of organize if if it has to put someone on the same tracker link for whatever reason. If there isn't enough links, it would kind of confirm who do you want to put on what link um with who. But for the most part, like the bot would kind of do the the sharing and the managing of the of the reps on the links um based on the availability. / Andy Bhiekham: ...I would copy that link that um the bot shoots out um from here and essentially / Andy Bhiekham: make sure that's in here. And um yeah, that's pretty much all.

items.topic: Pause/resume history lost on shared links
items.statement: Kobi said resuming by status change loses the history of when a link was paused and resumed, which makes reporting and allocation murky when reps share links. Jay agreed it can cause a real data reporting problem and said Ali has raised it with management before.
items.quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: ...the one thing I'm not particularly a fan of from like a data reporting perspective is like the resuming because you do lose the history of like when you last paused and then when you resumed, right? / Ali Nawaz: And that is it is definitely a problem. It gets a little uh annoying, / Kobi Kunasekaran: I think as long as like the reps have like a unique link per rep it's it doesn't matter but the moment they are sharing links that's when the reporting and allocation can get murky, right? If if we're not tracking when when one one person's link is being paused and the other person's / Jay: like to management as well about the fact that like it can cause a real data reporting problem when we don't have that information about when that when that person was paused. / Jay: That's definitely something like we agree with you on there for sure.

items.topic: Does Airtable store pause history
items.statement: It is unknown whether Airtable stores pause/resume dates. Andy thinks it shows only effective from/to; Jay thinks the bot can report pauses so the data is stored somewhere; Kobi noted 17 hidden fields may hold it.

So maybe it is being tracked on a field that we just don't see which which just might be the case.

items.topic: Previous Assignment field, same casino
items.statement: Jay said Previous Assignment populates automatically when a rep's assignment is replaced, always within the same casino (for example DraftKings GD to DraftKings CTM), so ops can see who was on a link when tracking reports arrive late.
items.quote: Jay: Previous assignment populates automatically. Um, so like for example, you could I can choose replace and replace someone's link with a different different assignment and it would uh it would it would basically say like okay so this guy was on DraftKings GD uh now he's on DraftKings uh CTM. / Jay: And the reason why we do that is so if uh we go want to go back and see who was on GD because our tracking reports come a little bit later than they supposed to. It's not hard for us to kind of like quickly see that at a glance.... / Kobi Kunasekaran: So, it it's previous assignment for the same casino though, right? Like not necessarily like uh they were previously on Proline and now they're on DraftKings. / Jay: Yeah. Yeah. It's always the same casino. Yeah. Yeah. No, we never do that.

items.topic: Priority book designation
items.statement: Client said books are marked priority or non-priority based on operator perks, benefits, relationship and profitability; higher profit books go to higher-volume reps and lower profit books to lower-volume reps.
items.quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: Okay. Priority book. What does that mean? / Jay: uh priority book just basic. So basically we have books that we deem as priority versus non-priority and we deem that based off of like uh the perks and benefits they give us and our are like a relationship with that operator. / Jay: There's like a delay. I didn't Sorry about that. I can just give you a quick like if it's low profit book, we give it to our low volume reps. / Jay: If it's a higher profit book, we give it to our higher volume reps....

items.topic: WhatsApp switch notices cause logging errors
items.statement: Client said reps are told of operator switches in WhatsApp, effective the minute the message is sent; reps forget or log late, which causes many incorrect logs.
items.quote: Jay: ...we do go into their chat and we we will tell them like DraftKings CTM has now been turned off. You are now on DraftKings GD. So effective that minute that we send that message, every single email they get, welcome email they get from there on forward, they would have to log on their sheet as DraftKings um like GD for example, right? Like whichever we updated them to. But you can imagine sometimes reps forget, sometimes those emails come in a little bit uh like sometimes those emails came in a little bit earlier and they didn't uh they didn't realize because they're logging a little late. / Jay: And so there's a lot of these like incorrect times and stuff like that.

items.topic: Signup complete only after proofs submitted
items.statement: Kobi summarized and Ali confirmed: clicks reach Salesforce or the PlayCan database, but completion is only verified when proofs (screenshots) arrive, mostly via WhatsApp, and are added to the player signup info.
items.quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: So the clicks yeah like as they click the studies it we that information is making it to either Salesforce or play can database right now but then you can't really verify that they did anything until you get the information from them uh generally through WhatsApp it seems that's when they submit the proof the screenshots and everything and you add that information into the players there's signup info and that's when you have enough they're considered like complete. / Ali Nawaz: Exactly.

items.statement: Andy said for compliance every client who participates in a study must complete a survey. Kobi asked if it is per person or per study; Andy confirmed it is once per account, after which the user can participate in several studies.
items.quote: Andy Bhiekham: every, um, client that participates in a study needs to complete a survey.... / Andy Bhiekham: So every every single user should essentially be doing a survey / Andy Bhiekham: um before participating in a / Andy Bhiekham: study. / Kobi Kunasekaran: Is it like per per person or is it per uh per study or like for like the clicking / Andy Bhiekham: Person. / Andy Bhiekham: would do the you would uh do the survey. So it's per per account I / Kobi Kunasekaran: but it's just the one survey that's needed to be considered like complete. / Andy Bhiekham: Correct. Correct. Correct. You can participate in several studies once you have an account.

Consistent with the doc's own gemini_disagreements entry that nothing was decided.

All right. Thanks,

items.topic: Airtable adopted only a few months ago
items.statement: Ali said WagerTech started using Airtable a couple of months ago. Before that, links were only turned on and off in PlayCan and tracked through messages, which he called a mess.
items.quote: Ali Nawaz: Yeah. So, so Kobe here for context, / Ali Nawaz: like a couple months ago was when we started incorporating Air Table. Before that, it was specifically just turning on and off on play can and kind of keeping track through our messages and it was obviously a mess like that, right?

items.topic: Stale Airtable statuses show duplicate active links
items.statement: While reviewing Andy's Airtable records, Ali said that if two different Caesars links show as active, it is because the record was not updated. Airtable link statuses can be stale.
items.quote: Ali Nawaz: if you if you see something active that like two different Caesars active there, / Ali Nawaz: that's obviously because we didn't uh update it,

items.topic: Shared link reassigned mid-month: review both reps
items.statement: Ali said that when links are shared and one rep is unassigned and another assigned to the same link within the same month, ops must look at both reps' numbers when reviewing tracking. With enough links, a tracker code stays with one rep until that rep is live again.
items.quote: Ali Nawaz: standpoint of here yeah if we have enough links we un we could assign one and unassign knowing that we're if nobody else would be assigned to that tracker code until he's back live again. But if we're sharing links, um if we're sharing links, then obviously you unassign the link. / Ali Nawaz: And if there's somebody else who's going to be using it instead of him, then we just have to make it clear that they're both on on the same one. So if they were if one was assigned and the other was unassigned within the same month, then we have to look at both of their numbers when we look at the uh tracking.

items.topic: No click visibility without Salesforce
items.statement: Ali said that without Salesforce, ops do not know when a player clicks a study; they act only when the referrer sends the welcome email and details. He said Salesforce click visibility is good for leads.
items.quote: Kobi Kunasekaran: Um when they click on the study, I think that's when like do you get any information back to know that they clicked on it or are you literally just waiting until like they send you the confirmation information to log the sign / Ali Nawaz: without Salesforce. Yeah, / Ali Nawaz: ...If they don't send that send us that detail, we kind of don't really do anything about it. Now that I mean with Salesforce, when you see people clicking, that's good for leads.
